text:
Marathon Petroleum stock ticked up 0.66% today after falling sharply over the prior two trading days. The modest gain came as oil prices pulled back from session highs following reports of potential talks to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a critical chokepoint for global crude shipments. Meanwhile, U.S. refineries are running at 94% capacity with oil inventories near 711 million barrels — suggesting steady operational demand even as geopolitical tensions around Iran remain elevated.

The stock's recent volatility reflects competing pressures on refiners. A proposed diesel export ban is generating significant concern in the industry because it could cut refinery production and ultimately raise fuel prices, which would hurt margins. At the same time, the threat of major supply disruptions from Iran tensions has kept crude prices elevated, which can support refinery economics — but only if those refineries can actually sell their products, making the export ban debate central to how refiners like Marathon will perform ahead.
